CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which activity is part of the primary sector?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Fishing directly uses aquatic biological resources.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is pastoral nomadism?
options: Moving with livestock in search of pasture and water
Growing rice in flooded fields only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Pastoral nomads move livestock to access grazing and water.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which factor can strongly influence the type of agriculture practised?
options: Only the number of television channels
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Climate, soil, relief, markets and technology influence agricultural systems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does mixed farming combine?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mixed farming integrates crops and livestock.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Manufacturing is classified as which economic activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Secondary activities process raw materials into goods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which factor may influence the location of an iron and steel industry?
options: Access to raw materials, energy and transport
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Heavy industries often consider raw materials, energy, markets and transport costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is cottage industry?
options: Small-scale production often based in homes or workshops
A large offshore oil platform only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cottage industries typically use small-scale, household or workshop production.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is an example of an agro-based industry?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cotton textile production processes an agricultural raw material.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is footloose industry?
options: An industry less tied to a specific raw-material location
An industry that must be beside a coal mine
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Footloose industries can locate in many places because transport costs or inputs are less location-bound.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why are industrial regions often associated with urban growth?
options: Urban growth occurs only in deserts
Factories create jobs and attract workers and services
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Industrial employment can attract workers and support services and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which activity is a high-technology industry?
options: Hand collection of forest products only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Semiconductor manufacturing relies on advanced technology and specialised skills.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does industrial agglomeration mean?
options: Concentration of industries in a particular area
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Agglomeration occurs when industries cluster and benefit from shared services or links.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a possible environmental impact of manufacturing?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Industrial activity can cause pollution unless controlled and managed.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is value addition in manufacturing?
options: Increasing a product's value by processing or transforming inputs
Moving a product without changing it
Reducing all goods to raw materials
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Processing can increase the economic value of raw materials.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is an example of a tertiary activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Tertiary activities provide services such as trade and transport.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which activity is commonly classified as quaternary?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Quaternary activities involve information, research and specialised knowledge.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Tourism is generally classified as what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Tourism includes services such as accommodation, transport and guiding.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which service connects producers with consumers by moving goods?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transport supports the movement of people and goods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is outsourcing?
options: Contracting work or services to an external provider
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Outsourcing transfers selected tasks to another organisation or provider.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which factor is important for the growth of information technology services?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: IT services depend on skills, connectivity and supportive infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a transnational corporation?
options: A company operating in more than one country
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transnational corporations conduct operations across national borders.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which service is part of the quinary sector in some classifications?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Some classifications use quinary for top-level decision-making and specialised services.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why do service industries often cluster in cities?
options: Cities provide markets, skilled labour and connectivity
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Urban areas can offer dense markets, labour pools and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does digital connectivity enable for service activities?
options: Remote communication and delivery of some services
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Digital networks allow some services and information to be delivered remotely.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which mode of transport is often economical for bulky goods over long inland distances?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Railways can move large quantities of freight efficiently over land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which transport mode is particularly important for international trade in heavy bulk cargo?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Ships carry large volumes of goods across oceans at relatively low unit cost.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a major advantage of air transport?
options: Lowest cost for every cargo type
Ability to carry unlimited bulk cheaply
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Air transport is fast, especially for passengers and high-value or time-sensitive cargo.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which infrastructure is essential for pipeline transport?
options: A railway station at every kilometre
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Pipelines move liquids and gases through connected pipes.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a port?
options: A place where ships load and unload people or cargo
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Ports connect maritime transport with land-based networks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is the role of communication networks?
options: Transmit information between people and places
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Communication systems transfer information through various media and technologies.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which technology supports satellite-based navigation?
options: Only a compass rose on a map
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Satellite navigation systems use signals from satellites to estimate position.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is containerisation?
options: Packing each item in a separate aircraft
Transporting goods in standardised containers across modes
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Standard containers facilitate transfers among ships, trains and trucks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which factor can limit transport access in mountainous regions?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Steep slopes and hazards can raise construction and maintenance costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: How can improved communication affect economic activity?
options: It can speed information exchange and coordination
It makes distance irrelevant in every situation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Communication can improve coordination but does not eliminate all geographic constraints.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is international trade?
options: Exchange of goods and services across national borders
Trade within a single household only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: International trade involves cross-border exchange.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a trade surplus?
options: When exports exceed imports in value
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A trade surplus occurs when the value of exports is greater than imports.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a service export?
options: Providing software services to a foreign client
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Services can be exported through tourism, IT, finance and other activities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a seaport's role in trade?
options: Handling cargo between sea and land transport
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Seaports are important nodes for international cargo movement.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does a country's balance of trade compare?
options: The value of goods exports and goods imports
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Balance of trade typically compares merchandise exports and imports.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why do countries trade with one another?
options: Resources, skills, costs and demand differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Differences in resources, productivity and demand create incentives for trade.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a free-trade agreement intended to do?
options: Reduce selected barriers to trade between participants
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Trade agreements can reduce tariffs or other barriers under agreed rules.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a possible risk of dependence on a narrow range of exports?
options: Vulnerability to price changes in those exports
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Export concentration can expose an economy to commodity-price and demand shocks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does globalisation generally increase?
options: Cross-border flows of goods, capital, services and information
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Globalisation often deepens international economic connections.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why are trade statistics interpreted carefully?
options: Definitions, prices and reporting methods can differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Data comparisons require attention to methods, coverage and time periods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: A resource becomes useful when it is accessible and has what?
options: Utility or value for human use
A large population nearby in every case
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Resources depend on usefulness, accessibility, technology and social needs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a renewable resource when managed sustainably?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Solar energy is naturally replenished on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a non-renewable fossil fuel?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Coal forms over geological timescales and is not replenished quickly.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does resource conservation mean?
options: Using every resource as fast as possible
Using resources carefully to reduce waste and depletion
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Conservation supports responsible use and long-term availability.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is sustainable development?
options: Maximising current extraction regardless of harm
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable development balances present needs, environment and future generations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which practice can reduce soil erosion?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Vegetation protects soil from runoff and wind.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is land degradation?
options: A decline in land's productive or ecological quality
An increase in every soil function
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Land degradation reduces soil quality, productivity or ecosystem functions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which factor can contribute to desertification?
options: Overgrazing and unsustainable land use in drylands
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Unsustainable land use can worsen degradation in dry regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is resource planning important?
options: Resources are unevenly distributed and need coordinated management
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Planning addresses uneven distribution, competing needs and sustainability.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is an example of human-made resource?
options: A wild forest untouched by people
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human-made resources are created or developed by people.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which process replenishes groundwater when water infiltrates the soil?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Infiltration and percolation can replenish aquifers.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a watershed?
options: An area draining water to a common outlet
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A watershed or drainage basin collects runoff to a shared outlet.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a potential benefit of rainwater harvesting?
options: Supplementing water supplies and reducing runoff
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Rainwater harvesting can store water and reduce some runoff.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a major concern associated with excessive groundwater extraction?
options: Rising river levels in every case
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Over-extraction can lower groundwater levels and affect wells and ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why can dams be controversial?
options: They are always built only for tourism
They can provide water and power but also displace people and alter ecosystems
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Dams have economic benefits and social and environmental costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which sector often uses a large share of freshwater withdrawals globally?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Agriculture is a major freshwater user in many regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is water scarcity?
options: When available water is insufficient for needs or access is limited
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Water scarcity can result from physical shortages or limited access and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which measure can improve irrigation efficiency?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Drip irrigation can deliver water close to plant roots and reduce losses.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What can cause river water pollution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sewage and industrial effluents can introduce contaminants to rivers.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is integrated water-resource management useful?
options: It considers competing users and environmental needs together
It focuses only on one user always
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Integrated management coordinates uses across sectors and catchments.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a metallic mineral?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Iron ore is a source of iron, a metal.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which energy source is fossil fuel based?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Petroleum is a non-renewable fossil fuel.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a major advantage of renewable energy sources?
options: They work identically in all locations
They are replenished naturally on human timescales
They have zero impact in every setting
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Renewables are replenished but still have siting, cost and environmental considerations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which mineral is commonly used in electrical wiring because of its conductivity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Copper is widely used in electrical wiring due to its conductivity.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is an ore?
options: A naturally occurring material from which a useful substance can be extracted economically
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: An ore contains a useful mineral or metal that can be extracted economically.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is a conventional non-renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Coal is a conventional fossil fuel and is non-renewable.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why can mining cause environmental problems?
options: It may disturb land, generate waste and pollute water
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mining can affect habitats, landforms and water quality if not managed well.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is energy conservation?
options: Burning more fuel for the same output
Reducing unnecessary energy use and improving efficiency
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Energy conservation reduces waste and demand.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which technology generates electricity directly from sunlight using photovoltaic cells?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Photovoltaic cells convert light into electrical energy.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is mineral distribution geographically uneven?
options: Geological processes vary from place to place
Mineral formation is random each day
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mineral deposits depend on geological history and conditions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is regional planning intended to address?
options: Only the shape of national flags
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Regional planning aims to respond to different needs and reduce disparities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is an example of a sustainable development goal at local level?
options: Improving water access while protecting the watershed
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable local development combines human needs and environmental protection.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is community participation important in development planning?
options: It guarantees every project has no cost
It eliminates the need for evidence
It brings local knowledge and affected people's priorities
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Participation can improve relevance, accountability and local ownership.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is an indicator used for in planning?
options: Measuring progress toward a defined objective
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Indicators help monitor whether a plan is meeting its goals.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why should planners consider environmental impact?
options: Projects can affect ecosystems, health and livelihoods
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Environmental assessment helps identify and manage potential impacts.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is decentralised planning?
options: Planning that gives meaningful roles to local levels of government
All decisions made only at a distant centre
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Decentralisation can align planning with local needs and knowledge.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which practice supports sustainable agriculture?
options: Removing all field boundaries and vegetation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Diversification and soil conservation can improve resilience and protect land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does inclusive development seek to do?
options: Ensure benefits and opportunities reach different social groups
Concentrate all benefits in one group
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Inclusive development considers access, equity and participation.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is monitoring necessary after a development project begins?
options: To identify progress, problems and needed adjustments
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Monitoring supports learning and timely correction.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is carrying capacity relevant to in planning?
options: Only the capacity of a truck
The number of pages in a report
The level of use an environment can sustain without unacceptable degradation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Carrying capacity helps assess sustainable pressure on resources and ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is urban waste management concerned with?
options: Collection, treatment and safe disposal or recovery of waste
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Waste management covers collection, processing, recycling and safe disposal.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a common source of urban air pollution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transport and industrial emissions can contribute to urban air pollution.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What does slum improvement generally aim to provide?
options: Better housing, sanitation, services and security of tenure where appropriate
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Upgrading aims to improve living conditions and essential services.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which is an example of water pollution?
options: Discharge of untreated sewage into a river
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Untreated sewage can contaminate water and spread pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is land-use conflict?
options: Competing demands for the same area of land
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Housing, farming, industry and conservation may compete for land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which practice can reduce flood risk in urban areas?
options: Building on every floodplain without planning
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Wetlands, drainage and sensible land-use planning can reduce some flood impacts.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is environmental justice important?
options: Environmental harms and benefits can be distributed unequally
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Environmental justice considers fairness in exposure, decision-making and access to benefits.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: What is a geographic information system (GIS) used for?
options: Storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: GIS supports mapping and analysis of geographically referenced data.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Which method can help assess local environmental conditions directly?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Field surveys collect direct observations and measurements.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Why is public awareness important in addressing environmental problems?
options: It can support informed choices and collective action
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Awareness can encourage participation, prevention and support for solutions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Human geography primarily studies relationships between humans and what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human geography examines interactions between people, places and environments.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which approach emphasises the unique character of individual places?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: The regional approach studies distinctive characteristics of places and regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does the term spatial distribution describe?
options: How phenomena are arranged across space
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Spatial distribution concerns where phenomena occur and how they are spread.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which of the following is a human-geography topic?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Migration is a key topic in population and human geography.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is a region in geography?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Regions are defined by shared physical, cultural, economic or other characteristics.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which tool is especially useful for representing spatial information?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Maps represent spatial relationships and geographic patterns.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does cultural landscape mean?
options: A landscape shaped by human activity and culture
A landscape untouched by any process
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cultural landscapes show how people shape and use places.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which factor can influence the location of settlements?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Water, relief, resources and accessibility can influence settlement locations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is globalisation in a geographical context?
options: Increasing connections among places and economies
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Globalisation links places through flows of goods, people, capital and information.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why do geographers use both maps and field observations?
options: They provide complementary spatial and on-site evidence
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Maps show spatial patterns, while fieldwork can verify and enrich local understanding.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Population density is commonly calculated as population divided by what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Population density is usually expressed as people per unit area.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is a physical factor influencing population distribution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Climate, relief, water and soils influence settlement and population distribution.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which process directly adds people to a population?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Births increase population size, while deaths and out-migration reduce it.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Natural population growth is the difference between what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Natural growth is determined by births minus deaths over a period.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is migration?
options: Movement of people from one place to another to live temporarily or permanently
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Migration involves a change of usual residence, though definitions vary by context.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is a common push factor for migration?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Push factors encourage people to leave a place, including unemployment or insecurity.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is an age-sex pyramid used to show?
options: Population structure by age and sex
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Age-sex pyramids depict population composition by age groups and sex.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: A population with a large proportion of children is likely to have what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A high child share indicates a relatively young population structure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does demographic transition describe?
options: Changes in birth and death rates as societies develop
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: The demographic transition model describes shifts in mortality and fertility patterns.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which measure is commonly used to compare fertility between populations?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Total fertility rate estimates the average number of children a woman would have under current age-specific rates.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Human development focuses on expanding people's what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human development includes health, education, living standards and people's opportunities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which indicator is commonly used to reflect health in the Human Development Index?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Life expectancy is an indicator of the health dimension in the HDI.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Literacy and years of schooling relate most directly to which human-development dimension?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Education indicators are used to represent the knowledge dimension.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Per capita income is calculated by dividing total income by what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Per capita income is average income per person.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why can income alone be an incomplete measure of development?
options: It is unrelated to living standards
It does not fully capture health, education or equality
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Development is multidimensional, so income alone cannot describe all aspects of well-being.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does sustainable human development seek to balance?
options: Present well-being and future generations' needs
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable development considers present needs and future generations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is an example of a social indicator?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Literacy rate reflects an aspect of educational attainment.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why do development levels vary among regions?
options: Every region has the same economy
Resources, institutions, history and access to services differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Development outcomes reflect multiple interacting geographic, social and economic factors.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which approach considers people's freedom to live lives they value?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: The capability approach focuses on people's real opportunities and freedoms.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Agriculture is classified as which type of economic activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Primary activities obtain resources directly from nature.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which activity involves raising livestock?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Animal husbandry involves breeding and caring for livestock.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Plantation agriculture typically involves what?
options: Large-scale cultivation of a single cash crop
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Plantations often specialise in commercial crops such as tea, coffee or rubber.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of subsistence agriculture?
options: Farming mainly to feed the farmer's household
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Subsistence farming primarily supports the farmer and household.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Commercial grain farming is often associated with what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Commercial grain farming often uses large holdings and mechanised methods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is shifting cultivation?
options: Growing crops in a permanent greenhouse only
Cultivating a plot for a period and then moving to another plot
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Shifting cultivation involves temporary cultivation followed by a move or fallow period.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which activity is part of the primary sector?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Fishing directly uses aquatic biological resources.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is pastoral nomadism?
options: Moving with livestock in search of pasture and water
Growing rice in flooded fields only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Pastoral nomads move livestock to access grazing and water.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which factor can strongly influence the type of agriculture practised?
options: Only the number of television channels
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Climate, soil, relief, markets and technology influence agricultural systems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What does mixed farming combine?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mixed farming integrates crops and livestock.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Manufacturing is classified as which economic activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Secondary activities process raw materials into goods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which factor may influence the location of an iron and steel industry?
options: Access to raw materials, energy and transport
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Heavy industries often consider raw materials, energy, markets and transport costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is cottage industry?
options: Small-scale production often based in homes or workshops
A large offshore oil platform only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cottage industries typically use small-scale, household or workshop production.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is an example of an agro-based industry?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cotton textile production processes an agricultural raw material.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is footloose industry?
options: An industry less tied to a specific raw-material location
An industry that must be beside a coal mine
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Footloose industries can locate in many places because transport costs or inputs are less location-bound.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why are industrial regions often associated with urban growth?
options: Urban growth occurs only in deserts
Factories create jobs and attract workers and services
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Industrial employment can attract workers and support services and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which activity is a high-technology industry?
options: Hand collection of forest products only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Semiconductor manufacturing relies on advanced technology and specialised skills.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What does industrial agglomeration mean?
options: Concentration of industries in a particular area
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Agglomeration occurs when industries cluster and benefit from shared services or links.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which is a possible environmental impact of manufacturing?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Industrial activity can cause pollution unless controlled and managed.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is value addition in manufacturing?
options: Reducing all goods to raw materials
Increasing a product's value by processing or transforming inputs
Moving a product without changing it
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Processing can increase the economic value of raw materials.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which is an example of a tertiary activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Tertiary activities provide services such as trade and transport.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which activity is commonly classified as quaternary?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Quaternary activities involve information, research and specialised knowledge.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Tourism is generally classified as what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Tourism includes services such as accommodation, transport and guiding.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which service connects producers with consumers by moving goods?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transport supports the movement of people and goods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is outsourcing?
options: Contracting work or services to an external provider
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Outsourcing transfers selected tasks to another organisation or provider.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which factor is important for the growth of information technology services?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: IT services depend on skills, connectivity and supportive infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is a transnational corporation?
options: A company operating in more than one country
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transnational corporations conduct operations across national borders.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which service is part of the quinary sector in some classifications?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Some classifications use quinary for top-level decision-making and specialised services.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why do service industries often cluster in cities?
options: Cities provide markets, skilled labour and connectivity
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Urban areas can offer dense markets, labour pools and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What does digital connectivity enable for service activities?
options: Remote communication and delivery of some services
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Digital networks allow some services and information to be delivered remotely.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which mode of transport is often economical for bulky goods over long inland distances?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Railways can move large quantities of freight efficiently over land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which transport mode is particularly important for international trade in heavy bulk cargo?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Ships carry large volumes of goods across oceans at relatively low unit cost.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is a major advantage of air transport?
options: Lowest cost for every cargo type
Ability to carry unlimited bulk cheaply
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Air transport is fast, especially for passengers and high-value or time-sensitive cargo.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which infrastructure is essential for pipeline transport?
options: A railway station at every kilometre
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Pipelines move liquids and gases through connected pipes.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is a port?
options: A place where ships load and unload people or cargo
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Ports connect maritime transport with land-based networks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is the role of communication networks?
options: Transmit information between people and places
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Communication systems transfer information through various media and technologies.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which technology supports satellite-based navigation?
options: Only a compass rose on a map
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Satellite navigation systems use signals from satellites to estimate position.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is containerisation?
options: Packing each item in a separate aircraft
Transporting goods in standardised containers across modes
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Standard containers facilitate transfers among ships, trains and trucks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which factor can limit transport access in mountainous regions?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Steep slopes and hazards can raise construction and maintenance costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: How can improved communication affect economic activity?
options: It makes distance irrelevant in every situation
It can speed information exchange and coordination
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Communication can improve coordination but does not eliminate all geographic constraints.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is international trade?
options: Trade within a single household only
Exchange of goods and services across national borders
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: International trade involves cross-border exchange.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is a trade surplus?
options: When exports exceed imports in value
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A trade surplus occurs when the value of exports is greater than imports.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which is a service export?
options: Providing software services to a foreign client
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Services can be exported through tourism, IT, finance and other activities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a seaport's role in trade?
options: Handling cargo between sea and land transport
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Seaports are important nodes for international cargo movement.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does a country's balance of trade compare?
options: The value of goods exports and goods imports
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Balance of trade typically compares merchandise exports and imports.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why do countries trade with one another?
options: Resources, skills, costs and demand differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Differences in resources, productivity and demand create incentives for trade.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is a free-trade agreement intended to do?
options: Reduce selected barriers to trade between participants
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Trade agreements can reduce tariffs or other barriers under agreed rules.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a possible risk of dependence on a narrow range of exports?
options: Vulnerability to price changes in those exports
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Export concentration can expose an economy to commodity-price and demand shocks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does globalisation generally increase?
options: Cross-border flows of goods, capital, services and information
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Globalisation often deepens international economic connections.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why are trade statistics interpreted carefully?
options: Definitions, prices and reporting methods can differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Data comparisons require attention to methods, coverage and time periods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: A resource becomes useful when it is accessible and has what?
options: Utility or value for human use
A large population nearby in every case
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Resources depend on usefulness, accessibility, technology and social needs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a renewable resource when managed sustainably?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Solar energy is naturally replenished on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which is a non-renewable fossil fuel?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Coal forms over geological timescales and is not replenished quickly.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What does resource conservation mean?
options: Using resources carefully to reduce waste and depletion
Using every resource as fast as possible
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Conservation supports responsible use and long-term availability.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is sustainable development?
options: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
Maximising current extraction regardless of harm
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable development balances present needs, environment and future generations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which practice can reduce soil erosion?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Vegetation protects soil from runoff and wind.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is land degradation?
options: A decline in land's productive or ecological quality
An increase in every soil function
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Land degradation reduces soil quality, productivity or ecosystem functions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which factor can contribute to desertification?
options: Overgrazing and unsustainable land use in drylands
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Unsustainable land use can worsen degradation in dry regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why is resource planning important?
options: Resources are unevenly distributed and need coordinated management
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Planning addresses uneven distribution, competing needs and sustainability.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of human-made resource?
options: A wild forest untouched by people
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human-made resources are created or developed by people.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which process replenishes groundwater when water infiltrates the soil?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Infiltration and percolation can replenish aquifers.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is a watershed?
options: An area draining water to a common outlet
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A watershed or drainage basin collects runoff to a shared outlet.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which is a potential benefit of rainwater harvesting?
options: Supplementing water supplies and reducing runoff
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Rainwater harvesting can store water and reduce some runoff.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a major concern associated with excessive groundwater extraction?
options: Rising river levels in every case
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Over-extraction can lower groundwater levels and affect wells and ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why can dams be controversial?
options: They are always built only for tourism
They can provide water and power but also displace people and alter ecosystems
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Dams have economic benefits and social and environmental costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which sector often uses a large share of freshwater withdrawals globally?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Agriculture is a major freshwater user in many regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is water scarcity?
options: When available water is insufficient for needs or access is limited
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Water scarcity can result from physical shortages or limited access and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which measure can improve irrigation efficiency?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Drip irrigation can deliver water close to plant roots and reduce losses.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What can cause river water pollution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sewage and industrial effluents can introduce contaminants to rivers.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why is integrated water-resource management useful?
options: It focuses only on one user always
It considers competing users and environmental needs together
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Integrated management coordinates uses across sectors and catchments.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which is a metallic mineral?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Iron ore is a source of iron, a metal.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which energy source is fossil fuel based?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Petroleum is a non-renewable fossil fuel.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is a major advantage of renewable energy sources?
options: They are replenished naturally on human timescales
They have zero impact in every setting
They work identically in all locations
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Renewables are replenished but still have siting, cost and environmental considerations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which mineral is commonly used in electrical wiring because of its conductivity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Copper is widely used in electrical wiring due to its conductivity.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is an ore?
options: A naturally occurring material from which a useful substance can be extracted economically
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: An ore contains a useful mineral or metal that can be extracted economically.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a conventional non-renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Coal is a conventional fossil fuel and is non-renewable.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why can mining cause environmental problems?
options: It may disturb land, generate waste and pollute water
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mining can affect habitats, landforms and water quality if not managed well.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is energy conservation?
options: Reducing unnecessary energy use and improving efficiency
Burning more fuel for the same output
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Energy conservation reduces waste and demand.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which technology generates electricity directly from sunlight using photovoltaic cells?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Photovoltaic cells convert light into electrical energy.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why is mineral distribution geographically uneven?
options: Geological processes vary from place to place
Mineral formation is random each day
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mineral deposits depend on geological history and conditions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is regional planning intended to address?
options: Only the shape of national flags
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Regional planning aims to respond to different needs and reduce disparities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is an example of a sustainable development goal at local level?
options: Improving water access while protecting the watershed
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable local development combines human needs and environmental protection.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why is community participation important in development planning?
options: It guarantees every project has no cost
It brings local knowledge and affected people's priorities
It eliminates the need for evidence
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Participation can improve relevance, accountability and local ownership.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is an indicator used for in planning?
options: Measuring progress toward a defined objective
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Indicators help monitor whether a plan is meeting its goals.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why should planners consider environmental impact?
options: Projects can affect ecosystems, health and livelihoods
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Environmental assessment helps identify and manage potential impacts.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is decentralised planning?
options: All decisions made only at a distant centre
Planning that gives meaningful roles to local levels of government
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Decentralisation can align planning with local needs and knowledge.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which practice supports sustainable agriculture?
options: Removing all field boundaries and vegetation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Diversification and soil conservation can improve resilience and protect land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What does inclusive development seek to do?
options: Concentrate all benefits in one group
Ensure benefits and opportunities reach different social groups
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Inclusive development considers access, equity and participation.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why is monitoring necessary after a development project begins?
options: To identify progress, problems and needed adjustments
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Monitoring supports learning and timely correction.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is carrying capacity relevant to in planning?
options: The number of pages in a report
Only the capacity of a truck
The level of use an environment can sustain without unacceptable degradation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Carrying capacity helps assess sustainable pressure on resources and ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is urban waste management concerned with?
options: Collection, treatment and safe disposal or recovery of waste
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Waste management covers collection, processing, recycling and safe disposal.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a common source of urban air pollution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transport and industrial emissions can contribute to urban air pollution.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What does slum improvement generally aim to provide?
options: Better housing, sanitation, services and security of tenure where appropriate
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Upgrading aims to improve living conditions and essential services.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is an example of water pollution?
options: Discharge of untreated sewage into a river
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Untreated sewage can contaminate water and spread pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is land-use conflict?
options: Competing demands for the same area of land
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Housing, farming, industry and conservation may compete for land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which practice can reduce flood risk in urban areas?
options: Building on every floodplain without planning
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Wetlands, drainage and sensible land-use planning can reduce some flood impacts.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why is environmental justice important?
options: Environmental harms and benefits can be distributed unequally
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Environmental justice considers fairness in exposure, decision-making and access to benefits.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is a geographic information system (GIS) used for?
options: Storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: GIS supports mapping and analysis of geographically referenced data.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which method can help assess local environmental conditions directly?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Field surveys collect direct observations and measurements.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why is public awareness important in addressing environmental problems?
options: It can support informed choices and collective action
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Awareness can encourage participation, prevention and support for solutions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Human geography primarily studies relationships between humans and what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human geography examines interactions between people, places and environments.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which approach emphasises the unique character of individual places?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: The regional approach studies distinctive characteristics of places and regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does the term spatial distribution describe?
options: How phenomena are arranged across space
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Spatial distribution concerns where phenomena occur and how they are spread.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which of the following is a human-geography topic?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Migration is a key topic in population and human geography.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is a region in geography?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Regions are defined by shared physical, cultural, economic or other characteristics.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which tool is especially useful for representing spatial information?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Maps represent spatial relationships and geographic patterns.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does cultural landscape mean?
options: A landscape untouched by any process
A landscape shaped by human activity and culture
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cultural landscapes show how people shape and use places.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which factor can influence the location of settlements?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Water, relief, resources and accessibility can influence settlement locations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is globalisation in a geographical context?
options: Increasing connections among places and economies
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Globalisation links places through flows of goods, people, capital and information.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why do geographers use both maps and field observations?
options: They provide complementary spatial and on-site evidence
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Maps show spatial patterns, while fieldwork can verify and enrich local understanding.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Population density is commonly calculated as population divided by what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Population density is usually expressed as people per unit area.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a physical factor influencing population distribution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Climate, relief, water and soils influence settlement and population distribution.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which process directly adds people to a population?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Births increase population size, while deaths and out-migration reduce it.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Natural population growth is the difference between what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Natural growth is determined by births minus deaths over a period.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is migration?
options: Movement of people from one place to another to live temporarily or permanently
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Migration involves a change of usual residence, though definitions vary by context.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is a common push factor for migration?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Push factors encourage people to leave a place, including unemployment or insecurity.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is an age-sex pyramid used to show?
options: Population structure by age and sex
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Age-sex pyramids depict population composition by age groups and sex.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: A population with a large proportion of children is likely to have what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A high child share indicates a relatively young population structure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does demographic transition describe?
options: Changes in birth and death rates as societies develop
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: The demographic transition model describes shifts in mortality and fertility patterns.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which measure is commonly used to compare fertility between populations?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Total fertility rate estimates the average number of children a woman would have under current age-specific rates.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Human development focuses on expanding people's what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human development includes health, education, living standards and people's opportunities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which indicator is commonly used to reflect health in the Human Development Index?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Life expectancy is an indicator of the health dimension in the HDI.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Literacy and years of schooling relate most directly to which human-development dimension?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Education indicators are used to represent the knowledge dimension.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Per capita income is calculated by dividing total income by what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Per capita income is average income per person.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why can income alone be an incomplete measure of development?
options: It does not fully capture health, education or equality
It is unrelated to living standards
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Development is multidimensional, so income alone cannot describe all aspects of well-being.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does sustainable human development seek to balance?
options: Present well-being and future generations' needs
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable development considers present needs and future generations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of a social indicator?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Literacy rate reflects an aspect of educational attainment.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why do development levels vary among regions?
options: Every region has the same economy
Resources, institutions, history and access to services differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Development outcomes reflect multiple interacting geographic, social and economic factors.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which approach considers people's freedom to live lives they value?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: The capability approach focuses on people's real opportunities and freedoms.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Agriculture is classified as which type of economic activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Primary activities obtain resources directly from nature.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which activity involves raising livestock?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Animal husbandry involves breeding and caring for livestock.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Plantation agriculture typically involves what?
options: Large-scale cultivation of a single cash crop
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Plantations often specialise in commercial crops such as tea, coffee or rubber.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is an example of subsistence agriculture?
options: Farming mainly to feed the farmer's household
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Subsistence farming primarily supports the farmer and household.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Commercial grain farming is often associated with what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Commercial grain farming often uses large holdings and mechanised methods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is shifting cultivation?
options: Cultivating a plot for a period and then moving to another plot
Growing crops in a permanent greenhouse only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Shifting cultivation involves temporary cultivation followed by a move or fallow period.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which activity is part of the primary sector?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Fishing directly uses aquatic biological resources.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is pastoral nomadism?
options: Moving with livestock in search of pasture and water
Growing rice in flooded fields only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Pastoral nomads move livestock to access grazing and water.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which factor can strongly influence the type of agriculture practised?
options: Only the number of television channels
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Climate, soil, relief, markets and technology influence agricultural systems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What does mixed farming combine?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mixed farming integrates crops and livestock.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Manufacturing is classified as which economic activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Secondary activities process raw materials into goods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which factor may influence the location of an iron and steel industry?
options: Access to raw materials, energy and transport
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Heavy industries often consider raw materials, energy, markets and transport costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is cottage industry?
options: Small-scale production often based in homes or workshops
A large offshore oil platform only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cottage industries typically use small-scale, household or workshop production.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of an agro-based industry?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Cotton textile production processes an agricultural raw material.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is footloose industry?
options: An industry that must be beside a coal mine
An industry less tied to a specific raw-material location
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Footloose industries can locate in many places because transport costs or inputs are less location-bound.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why are industrial regions often associated with urban growth?
options: Urban growth occurs only in deserts
Factories create jobs and attract workers and services
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Industrial employment can attract workers and support services and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which activity is a high-technology industry?
options: Hand collection of forest products only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Semiconductor manufacturing relies on advanced technology and specialised skills.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What does industrial agglomeration mean?
options: Concentration of industries in a particular area
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Agglomeration occurs when industries cluster and benefit from shared services or links.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which is a possible environmental impact of manufacturing?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Industrial activity can cause pollution unless controlled and managed.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is value addition in manufacturing?
options: Reducing all goods to raw materials
Increasing a product's value by processing or transforming inputs
Moving a product without changing it
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Processing can increase the economic value of raw materials.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which is an example of a tertiary activity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Tertiary activities provide services such as trade and transport.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which activity is commonly classified as quaternary?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Quaternary activities involve information, research and specialised knowledge.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Tourism is generally classified as what?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Tourism includes services such as accommodation, transport and guiding.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which service connects producers with consumers by moving goods?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transport supports the movement of people and goods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is outsourcing?
options: Contracting work or services to an external provider
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Outsourcing transfers selected tasks to another organisation or provider.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which factor is important for the growth of information technology services?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: IT services depend on skills, connectivity and supportive infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is a transnational corporation?
options: A company operating in more than one country
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transnational corporations conduct operations across national borders.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which service is part of the quinary sector in some classifications?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Some classifications use quinary for top-level decision-making and specialised services.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why do service industries often cluster in cities?
options: Cities provide markets, skilled labour and connectivity
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Urban areas can offer dense markets, labour pools and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What does digital connectivity enable for service activities?
options: Remote communication and delivery of some services
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Digital networks allow some services and information to be delivered remotely.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which mode of transport is often economical for bulky goods over long inland distances?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Railways can move large quantities of freight efficiently over land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which transport mode is particularly important for international trade in heavy bulk cargo?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Ships carry large volumes of goods across oceans at relatively low unit cost.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is a major advantage of air transport?
options: Ability to carry unlimited bulk cheaply
Lowest cost for every cargo type
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Air transport is fast, especially for passengers and high-value or time-sensitive cargo.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which infrastructure is essential for pipeline transport?
options: A railway station at every kilometre
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Pipelines move liquids and gases through connected pipes.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is a port?
options: A place where ships load and unload people or cargo
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Ports connect maritime transport with land-based networks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is the role of communication networks?
options: Transmit information between people and places
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Communication systems transfer information through various media and technologies.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which technology supports satellite-based navigation?
options: Only a compass rose on a map
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Satellite navigation systems use signals from satellites to estimate position.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is containerisation?
options: Packing each item in a separate aircraft
Transporting goods in standardised containers across modes
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Standard containers facilitate transfers among ships, trains and trucks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which factor can limit transport access in mountainous regions?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Steep slopes and hazards can raise construction and maintenance costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: How can improved communication affect economic activity?
options: It can speed information exchange and coordination
It makes distance irrelevant in every situation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Communication can improve coordination but does not eliminate all geographic constraints.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is international trade?
options: Exchange of goods and services across national borders
Trade within a single household only
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: International trade involves cross-border exchange.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a trade surplus?
options: When exports exceed imports in value
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A trade surplus occurs when the value of exports is greater than imports.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which is a service export?
options: Providing software services to a foreign client
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Services can be exported through tourism, IT, finance and other activities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is a seaport's role in trade?
options: Handling cargo between sea and land transport
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Seaports are important nodes for international cargo movement.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does a country's balance of trade compare?
options: The value of goods exports and goods imports
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Balance of trade typically compares merchandise exports and imports.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why do countries trade with one another?
options: Resources, skills, costs and demand differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Differences in resources, productivity and demand create incentives for trade.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is a free-trade agreement intended to do?
options: Reduce selected barriers to trade between participants
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Trade agreements can reduce tariffs or other barriers under agreed rules.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is a possible risk of dependence on a narrow range of exports?
options: Vulnerability to price changes in those exports
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Export concentration can expose an economy to commodity-price and demand shocks.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does globalisation generally increase?
options: Cross-border flows of goods, capital, services and information
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Globalisation often deepens international economic connections.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why are trade statistics interpreted carefully?
options: Definitions, prices and reporting methods can differ
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Data comparisons require attention to methods, coverage and time periods.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: A resource becomes useful when it is accessible and has what?
options: A large population nearby in every case
Utility or value for human use
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Resources depend on usefulness, accessibility, technology and social needs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is a renewable resource when managed sustainably?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Solar energy is naturally replenished on human timescales.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which is a non-renewable fossil fuel?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Coal forms over geological timescales and is not replenished quickly.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What does resource conservation mean?
options: Using resources carefully to reduce waste and depletion
Using every resource as fast as possible
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Conservation supports responsible use and long-term availability.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is sustainable development?
options: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
Maximising current extraction regardless of harm
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable development balances present needs, environment and future generations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which practice can reduce soil erosion?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Vegetation protects soil from runoff and wind.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is land degradation?
options: A decline in land's productive or ecological quality
An increase in every soil function
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Land degradation reduces soil quality, productivity or ecosystem functions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which factor can contribute to desertification?
options: Overgrazing and unsustainable land use in drylands
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Unsustainable land use can worsen degradation in dry regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why is resource planning important?
options: Resources are unevenly distributed and need coordinated management
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Planning addresses uneven distribution, competing needs and sustainability.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is an example of human-made resource?
options: A wild forest untouched by people
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Human-made resources are created or developed by people.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Which process replenishes groundwater when water infiltrates the soil?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Infiltration and percolation can replenish aquifers.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a watershed?
options: An area draining water to a common outlet
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: A watershed or drainage basin collects runoff to a shared outlet.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which is a potential benefit of rainwater harvesting?
options: Supplementing water supplies and reducing runoff
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Rainwater harvesting can store water and reduce some runoff.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is a major concern associated with excessive groundwater extraction?
options: Rising river levels in every case
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Over-extraction can lower groundwater levels and affect wells and ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why can dams be controversial?
options: They can provide water and power but also displace people and alter ecosystems
They are always built only for tourism
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Dams have economic benefits and social and environmental costs.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which sector often uses a large share of freshwater withdrawals globally?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Agriculture is a major freshwater user in many regions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is water scarcity?
options: When available water is insufficient for needs or access is limited
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Water scarcity can result from physical shortages or limited access and infrastructure.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which measure can improve irrigation efficiency?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Drip irrigation can deliver water close to plant roots and reduce losses.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What can cause river water pollution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sewage and industrial effluents can introduce contaminants to rivers.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Why is integrated water-resource management useful?
options: It considers competing users and environmental needs together
It focuses only on one user always
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Integrated management coordinates uses across sectors and catchments.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which is a metallic mineral?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Iron ore is a source of iron, a metal.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which energy source is fossil fuel based?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Petroleum is a non-renewable fossil fuel.
