CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is a major advantage of renewable energy sources?
options: They are replenished naturally on human timescales
They have zero impact in every setting
They work identically in all locations
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Renewables are replenished but still have siting, cost and environmental considerations.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which mineral is commonly used in electrical wiring because of its conductivity?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Copper is widely used in electrical wiring due to its conductivity.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is an ore?
options: A naturally occurring material from which a useful substance can be extracted economically
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: An ore contains a useful mineral or metal that can be extracted economically.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which is a conventional non-renewable energy source?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Coal is a conventional fossil fuel and is non-renewable.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why can mining cause environmental problems?
options: It may disturb land, generate waste and pollute water
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mining can affect habitats, landforms and water quality if not managed well.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is energy conservation?
options: Burning more fuel for the same output
Reducing unnecessary energy use and improving efficiency
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Energy conservation reduces waste and demand.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which technology generates electricity directly from sunlight using photovoltaic cells?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Photovoltaic cells convert light into electrical energy.

CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why is mineral distribution geographically uneven?
options: Mineral formation is random each day
Geological processes vary from place to place
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Mineral deposits depend on geological history and conditions.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What is regional planning intended to address?
options: Only the shape of national flags
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Regional planning aims to respond to different needs and reduce disparities.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of a sustainable development goal at local level?
options: Improving water access while protecting the watershed
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Sustainable local development combines human needs and environmental protection.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Why is community participation important in development planning?
options: It brings local knowledge and affected people's priorities
It guarantees every project has no cost
It eliminates the need for evidence
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Participation can improve relevance, accountability and local ownership.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is an indicator used for in planning?
options: Measuring progress toward a defined objective
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Indicators help monitor whether a plan is meeting its goals.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why should planners consider environmental impact?
options: Projects can affect ecosystems, health and livelihoods
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Environmental assessment helps identify and manage potential impacts.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is decentralised planning?
options: All decisions made only at a distant centre
Planning that gives meaningful roles to local levels of government
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Decentralisation can align planning with local needs and knowledge.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which practice supports sustainable agriculture?
options: Removing all field boundaries and vegetation
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Diversification and soil conservation can improve resilience and protect land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What does inclusive development seek to do?
options: Concentrate all benefits in one group
Ensure benefits and opportunities reach different social groups
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Inclusive development considers access, equity and participation.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why is monitoring necessary after a development project begins?
options: To identify progress, problems and needed adjustments
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Monitoring supports learning and timely correction.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Planning and Sustainable Development in India
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is carrying capacity relevant to in planning?
options: The number of pages in a report
The level of use an environment can sustain without unacceptable degradation
Only the capacity of a truck
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Carrying capacity helps assess sustainable pressure on resources and ecosystems.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is urban waste management concerned with?
options: Collection, treatment and safe disposal or recovery of waste
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Waste management covers collection, processing, recycling and safe disposal.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: What is a common source of urban air pollution?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Transport and industrial emissions can contribute to urban air pollution.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: What does slum improvement generally aim to provide?
options: Better housing, sanitation, services and security of tenure where appropriate
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Upgrading aims to improve living conditions and essential services.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: Which is an example of water pollution?
options: Discharge of untreated sewage into a river
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Untreated sewage can contaminate water and spread pathogens.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: What is land-use conflict?
options: Competing demands for the same area of land
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Housing, farming, industry and conservation may compete for land.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Which practice can reduce flood risk in urban areas?
options: Building on every floodplain without planning
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Wetlands, drainage and sensible land-use planning can reduce some flood impacts.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Revision check: Why is environmental justice important?
options: Environmental harms and benefits can be distributed unequally
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Environmental justice considers fairness in exposure, decision-making and access to benefits.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a geographic information system (GIS) used for?
options: Storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: GIS supports mapping and analysis of geographically referenced data.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Choose the best answer: Which method can help assess local environmental conditions directly?
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Field surveys collect direct observations and measurements.

CBSE 12 - Geography.topic: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
CBSE 12 - Geography.q: Quick review: Why is public awareness important in addressing environmental problems?
options: It can support informed choices and collective action
CBSE 12 - Geography.why: Awareness can encourage participation, prevention and support for solutions.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which feature is commonly associated with Harappan urban planning?
options: A planned street layout and drainage system
CBSE 12 - History.why: Harappan cities are noted for planned streets, drainage and organised settlements.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which material was widely used to make Harappan seals?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Many Harappan seals were made from steatite.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: The Great Bath is located at which Harappan site?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Great Bath is a well-known structure at Mohenjo-daro.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Harappan script is generally described as what?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Harappan script has not been conclusively deciphered.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which of the following was an important Harappan craft?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Harappan communities practised crafts such as bead-making and shell-working.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which Harappan site is associated with evidence often interpreted as a dockyard?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Lothal is often associated with a basin interpreted as a dockyard.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: What is a major source for reconstructing Harappan life?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Archaeologists study buildings, artefacts, bones and other material remains.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which animal appears frequently on Harappan seals?
CBSE 12 - History.why: A one-horned animal motif is common on Harappan seals.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: What can the distribution of Harappan weights suggest?
options: Standardised systems of measurement and exchange
CBSE 12 - History.why: Standardised weights suggest shared practices in measurement and trade.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Bricks, Beads and Bones: The Harappan Civilisation
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which evidence can help archaeologists study ancient diet?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Faunal and botanical remains provide evidence about food and subsistence.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which source is useful for studying early historic Indian political history?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Inscriptions can record rulers, donations, laws and political claims.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Ashoka's inscriptions are especially associated with the communication of what?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Ashoka used inscriptions to communicate dhamma and royal policies.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Punch-marked coins are important evidence for studying what?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Punch-marked coins provide evidence of early monetary exchange.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What was a janapada in early Indian history?
options: A territorial realm or settlement associated with a people
CBSE 12 - History.why: Janapadas developed as territorial units in early historic India.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which term refers to a large and powerful territorial state in early Indian history?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Mahajanapadas were major states described in early Indian sources.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Why are inscriptions important to historians?
options: They are all written by modern historians
They always tell the complete story without bias
They provide dated or datable statements from the past
CBSE 12 - History.why: Inscriptions are valuable primary sources, though they must be interpreted critically.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What was one important function of guilds in early towns?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Guilds could organise craftspeople and merchants.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which dynasty is associated with Ashoka?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Ashoka was a Mauryan ruler.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What do coins help historians investigate?
options: Trade, political authority and economic activity
CBSE 12 - History.why: Coins can offer evidence about rulers, exchange and economic life.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kings, Farmers and Towns: Early States and Economies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Why should historians compare multiple sources?
options: To ensure all sources say the same thing
To assess differences, bias and reliability
CBSE 12 - History.why: Comparing sources helps historians evaluate perspective and reliability.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which ancient text is a major source for studying kinship and social norms in early India?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Mahabharata is a major literary source, interpreted critically for social history.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: In historical studies, a patrilineal system traces descent through which line?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Patriliny traces descent through the male line.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What does endogamy mean?
options: Marriage within a specified social group
CBSE 12 - History.why: Endogamy refers to marriage within a defined group.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Why must historians read normative texts critically?
options: They describe ideals and rules, not necessarily everyday practice
They cannot be compared with archaeology
They are always modern eyewitness accounts
They contain no information at all
CBSE 12 - History.why: Normative texts often prescribe behaviour rather than directly recording all lived experience.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What is a genealogy?
options: A tax register for crops only
A record of family descent and relationships
CBSE 12 - History.why: Genealogies trace family lines and relationships.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which concept refers to social divisions based on birth and inherited status?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Caste is a form of social stratification often linked to birth and inherited status.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Why are inscriptions recording donations to religious institutions useful?
options: They show only modern school attendance
They can reveal social groups, patrons and economic relationships
CBSE 12 - History.why: Donative inscriptions can identify donors and illuminate social relations.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What can differences between prescriptive texts and inscriptions reveal?
options: Differences between social ideals and historical practices
CBSE 12 - History.why: Comparing evidence can show how actual practices differed from stated norms.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: What is a primary historical source?
options: Evidence produced in or close to the period being studied
CBSE 12 - History.why: Primary sources originate in the period or context under investigation.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Kinship, Caste and Class: Early Societies
CBSE 12 - History.q: Why is the Mahabharata useful but challenging as a historical source?
options: It was written as a modern census
It contains layered traditions and was composed over time
CBSE 12 - History.why: The epic developed over time, so its layers and context require critical analysis.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: The Buddha is associated with the founding of which religious tradition?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Buddha's teachings became central to Buddhism.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: Mahavira is a major teacher associated with which tradition?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Mahavira is recognised as a key teacher in Jain tradition.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: What is a stupa primarily associated with?
options: Enshrining relics and commemorating Buddhist traditions
CBSE 12 - History.why: Stupas are Buddhist monuments often associated with relics and worship.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: What does the term ahimsa mean?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Ahimsa, or non-violence, is important in Jain and other Indian traditions.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: Why are religious buildings useful to historians?
options: They reveal patronage, beliefs, art and social activity
CBSE 12 - History.why: Architecture and inscriptions can reveal religious and social history.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: What was the Sangha in Buddhist tradition?
options: The community of monks and nuns
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Sangha is the Buddhist monastic community.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: Which source can help reconstruct early religious beliefs?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Historians use several kinds of evidence to study beliefs and practices.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: What is an important feature of many Buddhist narratives about the Buddha's past lives?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Jataka stories recount narratives associated with the Buddha's previous births.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings: Cultural Developments
CBSE 12 - History.q: Patronage of religious monuments often came from whom?

options: Gandhi suspended the movement after violence
It began the Quit India Movement
CBSE 12 - History.why: Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement after the violent incident in 1922.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
CBSE 12 - History.q: Revision check: Why are letters and speeches useful for studying Gandhi's politics?
options: They reveal arguments, strategies and changing positions
They always represent every Indian's opinion
CBSE 12 - History.why: Letters and speeches help trace political thought and strategy.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
CBSE 12 - History.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What was one aim of the Civil Disobedience Movement?
options: To openly break selected colonial laws as protest
CBSE 12 - History.why: Civil disobedience challenged colonial authority through deliberate law-breaking.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
CBSE 12 - History.q: Choose the best answer: Why should historians study oral histories of the freedom struggle?
options: They preserve personal memories and local experiences
They are always exact in every detail
CBSE 12 - History.why: Oral histories preserve experiences but should be contextualised and compared.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement
CBSE 12 - History.q: Quick review: Which event is associated with the end of British colonial rule in India?
CBSE 12 - History.why: British colonial rule ended when India became independent in 1947.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Revision check: In which year was British India partitioned and India became independent?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Partition accompanied independence in 1947.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What does oral history help historians understand about Partition?
options: Personal memories, displacement and lived experiences
CBSE 12 - History.why: Oral testimonies preserve experiences of migration, violence and loss.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Choose the best answer: What was a major consequence of Partition?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Partition caused large-scale displacement and violence.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Quick review: Why do historians use letters and family memories about Partition?
options: To understand personal and local experiences
CBSE 12 - History.why: Personal sources reveal experiences often absent from official records.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Revision check: Why can memories of Partition differ among people?
options: Everyone witnessed the same events identically
People experienced events from different places and positions
CBSE 12 - History.why: Experiences and later recollections vary across individuals and communities.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is a refugee in the context of Partition?
options: A person forced to leave home due to upheaval or insecurity
CBSE 12 - History.why: Partition displaced people who fled violence and uncertainty.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Choose the best answer: Why should oral testimonies be handled sensitively?
options: They may recount trauma and personal loss
CBSE 12 - History.why: Sensitive handling respects witnesses and the effects of traumatic experiences.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Quick review: What can administrative records reveal about Partition?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Administrative records document official responses but may omit personal experiences.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: Revision check: Why is Partition history more than a study of borders?
options: It includes social, emotional and human consequences
CBSE 12 - History.why: Partition affected families, communities, livelihoods and identities beyond territorial division.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Understanding Partition
CBSE 12 - History.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: How can historians build a fuller account of Partition?
options: Compare oral histories, official documents and other evidence
CBSE 12 - History.why: Multiple kinds of evidence provide a more nuanced historical account.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Choose the best answer: When did the Constituent Assembly of India first meet?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Quick review: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
CBSE 12 - History.why: B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Revision check: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: On which date did the Constitution of India come into effect?
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Choose the best answer: Why were debates in the Constituent Assembly important?
options: They had no effect on the Constitution
They recorded arguments about rights, institutions and governance
CBSE 12 - History.why: Assembly debates show how constitutional provisions were discussed and justified.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Quick review: What is the Preamble of the Constitution?
options: An introductory statement of constitutional ideals and purposes
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Preamble states guiding values and objectives of the Constitution.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Revision check: Which principle means the state does not establish an official religion and treats religions according to constitutional principles?
CBSE 12 - History.why: Secularism is a constitutional principle concerning the relationship between state and religion.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: CBSE Class 12 practice: What is universal adult franchise?
options: The right of adult citizens to vote subject to constitutional and legal rules
CBSE 12 - History.why: Universal adult franchise extends voting rights to adult citizens under the law.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Choose the best answer: Why was a written Constitution important to independent India?
options: It established institutions, powers and rights in a common framework
CBSE 12 - History.why: The Constitution sets out the structure of government and fundamental principles.

CBSE 12 - History.topic: Framing the Constitution
CBSE 12 - History.q: Quick review: Why should historians study the Constituent Assembly debates?
options: They reveal the reasoning behind constitutional choices
CBSE 12 - History.why: Debates help explain competing ideas and decisions during constitution-making.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Psychology studies individual differences in abilities, traits, and behaviour using systematic methods.
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: The chapter examines intelligence, aptitude, personality, and individual differences.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which term refers to the capacity to learn, reason, solve problems, and adapt?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Intelligence broadly involves learning, reasoning, problem solving, and adaptation.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which test is designed to assess a person's potential to learn a specific skill?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Aptitude tests estimate potential to acquire skills or perform in a domain.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What does an achievement test primarily measure?
options: What a person has learned or mastered
Potential to learn any skill in the future
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Achievement tests assess learned knowledge or skills.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which approach views intelligence as involving multiple relatively distinct abilities?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Gardner's theory proposes several forms of intelligence, though theories differ in evidence and acceptance.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is emotional intelligence concerned with?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Emotional intelligence involves understanding and regulating emotions in oneself and others.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which is an example of a non-verbal intelligence test format?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Non-verbal tests use figures or patterns to reduce dependence on language.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What does a percentile rank indicate?
options: The percentage of a reference group scoring at or below a given score
The exact percentage of questions answered correctly in all cases
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Percentile rank locates a score relative to a comparison group.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is personality?
options: A relatively enduring pattern of characteristics influencing behaviour
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Personality refers to relatively stable patterns of thinking, feeling, and behaving.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which approach explains personality through unconscious conflicts and early experiences?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Psychodynamic theories emphasize unconscious processes and early experiences.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Who is associated with the psychoanalytic theory of personality?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Freud developed psychoanalytic theory, emphasizing unconscious processes.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: In Freud's model, which structure operates according to the pleasure principle?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: The id seeks immediate gratification and is described as operating by the pleasure principle.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: In Freud's model, which structure mediates between impulses and reality?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: The ego follows the reality principle and mediates demands of the id, superego, and environment.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which approach emphasizes personal growth, free will, and self-actualisation?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Humanistic theories emphasize agency, growth, and fulfilment of potential.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is self-concept?
options: A score on one exam only
A person's perception and understanding of themselves
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Self-concept includes beliefs and perceptions about one's own attributes and identity.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is a personality trait?
options: A relatively consistent characteristic used to describe behaviour
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Traits are relatively stable dimensions used to describe individual differences.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which of the following is a commonly discussed defence mechanism?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Rationalisation involves giving a plausible explanation that conceals an uncomfortable motive or feeling.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is stress?
options: A response to demands or challenges appraised as taxing or exceeding resources
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Stress arises when demands are appraised as challenging or exceeding coping resources.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which type of stress is associated with positive challenge and motivation?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Eustress is often used for stress experienced as motivating or beneficial.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is coping?
options: Efforts to manage demands and the emotions associated with them
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Coping includes cognitive and behavioural efforts to handle stressful demands.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which coping strategy focuses on changing the source of a problem?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Problem-focused coping aims to address or change the stressor itself.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which coping strategy mainly aims to regulate emotional responses to stress?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Emotion-focused coping manages feelings associated with the stressor.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which practice can help reduce stress through focused attention and calm awareness?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Mindfulness practices may support attention and stress regulation.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is resilience?
options: The ability to adapt and recover in the face of adversity
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Resilience is the capacity to adapt and recover amid difficulties.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is a psychological disorder generally characterized by?
options: A clinically significant disturbance in cognition, emotion regulation, or behaviour
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Clinical definitions focus on significant disturbances and consider distress, dysfunction, and context.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which anxiety disorder involves excessive worry across multiple areas of life?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Generalized anxiety disorder involves persistent, excessive anxiety and worry across domains.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: A specific phobia involves:
options: Loss of memory after every event
Marked fear of a particular object or situation
Only a fear of all social contact
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Specific phobia is an intense fear response to a particular object or situation.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which condition is characterized by intrusive thoughts and/or repetitive compulsions?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: OCD involves obsessions, compulsions, or both that cause distress or impairment.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which mood disorder can involve episodes of depression and mania or hypomania?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Bipolar disorders involve mood episodes that include mania or hypomania and often depression.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which is a common symptom of a depressive episode?
options: Persistent low mood or loss of interest
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Depression can involve low mood or loss of interest along with other symptoms.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is a hallucination?
options: A perception-like experience without an external stimulus of the relevant kind
A firmly held false belief only
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Hallucinations are perception-like experiences occurring without a corresponding external stimulus.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is a delusion?
options: A strongly held belief not adequately explained by shared cultural context and resistant to contrary evidence
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Delusions are fixed beliefs that are not explained by a person's cultural context.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Why is professional assessment important when someone experiences persistent mental health difficulties?
options: It helps clarify symptoms and guide appropriate support or treatment
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Qualified assessment helps distinguish possible causes and identify suitable care.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is psychotherapy?
options: A structured psychological treatment using psychological methods
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Psychotherapy uses psychological methods to help address emotional, behavioural, or mental health concerns.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which therapy approach focuses on identifying and changing unhelpful thoughts and behaviours?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: CBT examines relationships among thoughts, feelings, and behaviours and develops more helpful patterns.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is the therapeutic alliance?
options: The collaborative working relationship between therapist and client
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: The therapeutic alliance includes agreement on goals and tasks and a trusting working relationship.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is systematic desensitisation commonly used to treat?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Systematic desensitisation pairs relaxation with gradual exposure in a planned hierarchy.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is the goal of rehabilitation in mental health care?
options: Supporting functioning, recovery, and participation in daily life
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Rehabilitation aims to improve functioning, independence, and participation.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is a group therapy setting?
options: A test taken alone with no interaction
A therapist works with several clients in a structured group
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Group therapy uses group interaction and professional facilitation to support therapeutic goals.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is an attitude?
options: A learned tendency to evaluate an object, person, or issue positively or negatively
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Attitudes include evaluations and can influence thought, feeling, and behaviour.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: Which are commonly described as components of attitude?
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: The tripartite model includes beliefs/thoughts, feelings, and behavioural tendencies.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is a stereotype?
options: A generalized belief about members of a group
A fair assessment of every individual
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Stereotypes are generalized beliefs about groups that may oversimplify differences.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is prejudice?
options: A preconceived evaluation or attitude toward a person based on group membership
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Prejudice involves evaluative attitudes, often negative, toward people based on group membership.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is discrimination?
options: Unfair behaviour or treatment based on group membership
A belief with no action in every case
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Discrimination refers to behaviour or unequal treatment toward people based on group membership.

options: A kind of visual illusion only
Explaining the causes of behaviour or events
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Attribution involves inferring causes of behaviour, such as personal or situational factors.

options: Adjusting behaviour or opinions to align with group norms or expectations
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Conformity is changing responses to match group norms or pressure.

options: Changing behaviour in response to a direct request
Changing behaviour only under physical force
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Compliance involves responding to a request, without necessarily changing private beliefs.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.q: What is obedience in social psychology?
options: Following a directive from an authority figure
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Obedience is behaviour in response to commands from a perceived authority.

options: A group becomes a random sample
A group discussion strengthens the group's initial tendency or position
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Group polarisation can lead group members toward a more extreme version of the initial inclination.

options: A decision-making pattern where desire for group agreement suppresses critical evaluation
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Groupthink can discourage dissent and realistic evaluation of alternatives.

Practical, humane support to people affected by distressing events
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Psychological first aid emphasizes safety, practical help, listening, and connection to support.

CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Positive psychology studies positive experiences, strengths, and conditions supporting flourishing.

It removes the need for practice
CBSE 12 - Psychology.why: Adequate sleep supports cognitive performance, emotional regulation, and health.

Only a list of correct facts

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What does social exclusion mean?
options: A person's choice of clothing only
Processes that restrict groups' participation in social, economic, or political life

CBSE 12 - Sociology.topic: Patterns of Social Inequality and Exclusion
CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is untouchability?
options: A discriminatory practice historically associated with caste hierarchy

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a minority group in sociology?

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What does gender refer to in sociological analysis?
options: Socially constructed roles, expectations, and relations associated with sex categories

CBSE 12 - Sociology.topic: Patterns of Social Inequality and Exclusion
CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is affirmative action intended to do?
options: Address historical disadvantage and improve access to opportunities
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Affirmative action policies seek to address structural disadvantage and unequal opportunity.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is cultural diversity?
options: A society with only one cultural expression
The presence of different cultural traditions, languages, beliefs, and practices
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Cultural diversity includes differences in language, religion, customs, and ways of life.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is communalism in the Indian context commonly associated with?
options: Political or social mobilization around religious identities in antagonistic ways

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What does secularism generally mean in the Indian constitutional context?
options: The state does not establish one official religion and protects religious freedom under constitutional principles

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is regionalism?
options: Identification with or political emphasis on a particular region
A method of drawing a family tree
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Regionalism emphasizes regional identity, interests, or claims.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is industrialisation?
options: The growth of industrial production and related economic and social transformation
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Industrialisation changes work, production, settlement, and social relations.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is urbanisation?
options: Only a change in household size
A decline in every city population
An increase in the share of population living in urban areas and expansion of urban life
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Urbanisation involves growth of urban populations and urban ways of life.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is colonialism?
options: A system in which one power controls another territory and its people
A form of local self-government in all cases
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Colonialism involves political and economic domination by an external power.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is globalisation?
options: The complete isolation of all countries
Increasing interconnectedness of economies, societies, cultures, and communication across borders
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Globalisation increases cross-border flows of goods, capital, people, information, and cultural influences.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is Sanskritisation, a concept associated with M. N. Srinivas?
options: A process in which a lower-status group adopts practices of a higher-status group to seek status mobility
A theory of population growth only
A type of language translation software
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Sanskritisation describes status mobility through adoption of practices associated with locally dominant or higher-status groups.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is westernisation in Indian sociology commonly used to describe?
options: The disappearance of all Indian traditions
Changes associated with contact with Western institutions, ideas, and practices
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: The concept describes social and cultural changes linked to Western influence.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is agrarian structure concerned with?
options: Land ownership, cultivation, labour, and rural power relations
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Agrarian structure concerns land, agricultural production, labour, and related power relations.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is landlessness?
options: A condition in which a household or person does not own agricultural land
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Landlessness can shape livelihood security, labour relations, and rural inequality.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is the Green Revolution commonly associated with?
options: Higher agricultural yields through improved seeds, irrigation, fertilizers, and related inputs
A movement to replace all farming with factories
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: The Green Revolution increased yields in selected crops and regions through technological changes, with uneven effects.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is organised-sector employment generally associated with?
options: Formal rules, records, and greater legal or institutional regulation
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: The organised sector typically has more formal regulation and employment arrangements than the unorganised sector.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is the unorganised sector often characterized by?
options: Informal work arrangements and limited social security
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Unorganised work often involves insecurity, informal contracts, and limited protections.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a trade union?
options: An organisation formed by workers to represent their collective interests
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Trade unions represent workers in matters such as wages, conditions, and rights.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a social movement?
options: Collective action seeking or resisting social change
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Social movements involve sustained collective efforts around shared goals or grievances.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a reform movement?
options: A movement that can never seek change
A movement seeking change in particular practices or institutions
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Reform movements seek to change specific social practices or institutions.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a revolutionary movement generally intended to do?
options: Bring about fundamental transformation of a social or political order
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Revolutionary movements aim for deep structural change.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is environmentalism?
options: Collective concern and action to protect the environment
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Environmental movements address environmental protection, justice, and sustainability.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a women's movement?
options: Collective action addressing gender inequality and women's rights
A type of urban planning only
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Women's movements have challenged gender-based inequality and sought social, legal, and political change.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a tribal movement often concerned with?
options: Land, forest rights, identity, autonomy, and livelihood
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Many tribal movements concern resource rights, displacement, cultural identity, and self-determination.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a peasant movement?
options: Collective action by cultivators or rural producers around agrarian issues
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Peasant movements may address land, rents, prices, debt, labour, or state policy.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is population density?
options: The number of people per unit area
The percentage of women in a population
The number of births in a year only
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Population density is commonly measured as people per unit of land area.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is life expectancy at birth?
options: The number of children per woman
The average number of years a newborn is expected to live under current mortality conditions
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Life expectancy at birth summarizes mortality conditions for a population.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is the sociological imagination commonly associated with C. Wright Mills?
options: Explaining all behaviour only by biology
Connecting personal experiences with wider social structures and historical conditions
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Sociological imagination links individual biographies with social and historical contexts.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a matrilineal system?
options: Authority always held by every woman in all settings
Descent or inheritance traced through the mother's line
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Matrilineality traces descent through the maternal line; it does not automatically mean matriarchy.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is a patrilineal system?
options: Descent or inheritance traced through the father's line
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Patrilineality traces descent through the paternal line.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is deindustrialisation?
options: A decline in industrial activity or industrial employment in a region or economy
An increase in every factory's workforce
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Deindustrialisation refers to reduced industrial output or employment, often with wider social effects.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is outsourcing?
options: Contracting some work or services to an external provider
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Outsourcing transfers certain activities to external firms or providers.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is assimilation in discussions of cultural diversity?
options: A process in which a group adopts features of another dominant culture
A complete increase in linguistic diversity in every case
CBSE 12 - Sociology.why: Assimilation describes convergence toward another culture, though actual processes vary and may be unequal.

CBSE 12 - Sociology.topic: Patterns of Social Inequality and Exclusion
CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: What is intersectionality used to examine?

Only one social category in isolation in every case

The absence of all social groups
A single uniform way of life

options: The structured ranking of groups or people in a society

People who interact and share a sense of belonging or common identity
A list of names without interaction

options: Population size, composition, distribution, and change

options: The actual reproductive performance of a population
The number of roads in a city

CBSE 12 - Sociology.q: For Class XII Sociology, identify the correct answer: What does mortality refer to? Select the best answer.

A change in a person's mood

People typically outside working ages with those in working ages
